name: The Saltmarch
blurb: A drowning coast of stilt-towns and tide-lore, where the sea takes a little more land every year and the things it leaves behind do not always stay dead.
author: Open Dungeon Master
inspiredBy: An original setting written for this project. Free to copy, change, and use as the starting point for your own world pack.
dmFlavor: Tone: waterlogged dark fantasy on a coast that is losing. The sea is rising a hand's width a year and nobody can stop it, so every settlement is temporary and everyone knows it. Magic here is tidal and borrowed: it works better at high water, it always wants something back, and a caster who takes too much starts to smell of brine. Keep the horror quiet and material. Rot, salt, debt, a bell ringing in a town that drowned a decade ago. Threats are rarely evil so much as hungry or owed. Never present a clean victory over the water itself; the party can save people, buy time, and settle debts, but the tide is not a villain to be defeated. Reward preparation, local knowledge, and treating the drowned with respect.
mapStyle: weathered nautical chart, salt-stained vellum, depth soundings and tide marks, muted blue-grey and rust ink
portraitStyle: damp coastal portrait, oilskin and rope, grey overcast light, salt-cracked skin
nameHints: Wet, consonant-heavy coastal names (Brackwater, Old Fennow, the Gullet, Marrow Quay).
raceHint: The marsh peoples are mostly human, marsh-kin, and the reptilian folk of the deep channels. Describe someone by their town and their trade before their blood.
theme: A sinking coast of stilt-towns, tide-debts, and things the water gives back
premise: Old Fennow has three years of dry land left, maybe four. The Tidewardens who were supposed to hold the seawall have not been paid since spring, the salvage guilds are already pricing the town's bones, and last week the bell of a settlement that drowned eleven years ago started ringing again at low water. Somebody has to walk out there and find out who is pulling the rope.

races.name: Marchfolk
races.blurb: Coast-born and stubborn about it. They have moved their house inland twice already and will do it again.

races.name: Quayborn
races.blurb: Raised in the stilt-towns proper, on rope ladders and tide tables, with one useful trick learned young.

races.name: Fennow Small-folk
races.blurb: Marsh halflings who eat what the channels give and are notoriously hard to poison.

races.name: Channel-kin
races.blurb: Cold-blooded people of the deep waterways, older here than any town, and unsentimental about all of them.

races.name: Shellback
races.blurb: Slow, long-lived salvagers who remember the coastline as it was two generations ago.

races.name: Tidetouched
races.blurb: Born during a spring flood with the water still in them. Their debts to it come due early.

races.name: Breakwater Kin
races.blurb: The families who build and rebuild the seawall, and who are never thanked for it.

races.name: Fen-warden
races.blurb: Great quiet people of the reed country who tend the marsh the way others tend a garden.

races.name: Pileworker
races.blurb: Come down from the hill holds to drive the foundations, and stayed for the wages.

races.name: Reedwalker
races.blurb: Elves of the drowned forest, who still name trees that have been underwater for a century.

races.name: Debt-marked
races.blurb: Someone in the family line borrowed from the wrong tide, and the mark came due on you.

races.name: Sluice-rat
races.blurb: Small, fast, and employed in every drain and culvert on the coast.

backgrounds.name: Channel Pilot
backgrounds.blurb: You know which of the marked routes still exist and which the charts are lying about.

backgrounds.name: Wall-holder
backgrounds.blurb: You put your shoulder to a breach during a spring flood and the town has not forgotten.

backgrounds.name: Wreck-picker
backgrounds.blurb: Salvage is legal. Getting to the wreck before the guild is not.

backgrounds.name: Ropewright
backgrounds.blurb: Everything on this coast is held up by rope, and you are the reason it holds.

backgrounds.name: Bell-keeper
backgrounds.blurb: You ring for the drowned at low water so they know somebody still counts them.

backgrounds.name: Reed Runner
backgrounds.blurb: You carry messages across marsh nobody else will cross on foot.

backgrounds.name: Light-tender
backgrounds.blurb: You kept a lamp burning alone on a rock for years, and something out there noticed.

backgrounds.name: Mudlark
backgrounds.blurb: You grew up working the low-tide flats for whatever the water left.

backgrounds.name: Tide-scholar
backgrounds.blurb: You keep the water tables and the drowning records, and you know what the numbers mean.

backgrounds.name: Tidewarden
backgrounds.blurb: You held the seawall for a wage that stopped arriving.

classes.name: Tidewarden
classes.blurb: Trained to hold a breach in the dark with the water coming in.

classes.name: Wreck-diver
classes.blurb: Goes into the flooded rooms nobody else will, and comes back with the good part.

classes.name: Channel Runner
classes.blurb: Reads the water the way other people read a road.

classes.name: Fen-warden
classes.blurb: Serves the marsh itself, which is not the same as serving the people on it.

classes.name: Bell-keeper
classes.blurb: Counts the drowned and asks the deep water for small mercies.

classes.name: Debt-holder
classes.blurb: Borrowed from something under the water and is very much still paying.

classes.name: Tide-scholar
classes.blurb: Treats magic as a set of tables: what the water will lend, when, and at what rate.

classes.name: Breakwater
classes.blurb: The one they send at the thing that got over the wall.

classes.name: Salt-singer
classes.blurb: Keeps the working songs that keep a crew alive, and the gossip that keeps a town honest.

classes.name: Oathkeeper of the Wall
classes.blurb: Swore to hold the line long after the wage for holding it stopped.

classes.name: Pumpwright
classes.blurb: Keeps the drainage engines running, which is closer to sorcery than anyone admits.

classes.name: Stillwater Adept
classes.blurb: Learned patience from the tide and hits like it too.

spells.name: Draw the Water Out
spells.blurb: Pulling brine from a wound, which stings considerably more than the injury did.

spells.name: Call Them Back
spells.blurb: A name shouted across the flats before the water finishes the job.

spells.name: Lamp-touch
spells.blurb: A cold steady glow that fog does not swallow.

spells.name: Tide-sense
spells.blurb: A borrowed moment of knowing which way the water is going.

spells.name: Fair Passage
spells.blurb: A small favour asked of the deep water, and generally granted.

spells.name: Breakwater
spells.blurb: A hand's width of hardened air, in the shape of a wall nobody built.

spells.name: Haar
spells.blurb: The coastal fog that rolls in from nowhere, called deliberately for once.

spells.name: Reckon the Tide
spells.blurb: The most useful working on this coast, and the most quietly resented.

spells.name: Sparkshot
spells.blurb: Struck off a flint charm, because open flame is precious in a wet country.

spells.name: Surge
spells.blurb: A wave that arrives without water, and knocks the wind out of a room.

spells.name: Slip the Channel
spells.blurb: A step that goes through the water table and comes out somewhere close.

spells.name: Fogging
spells.blurb: The particular grey nothing of a shape seen through haar.

spells.name: Deep Water
spells.blurb: The dark of eleven fathoms down, brought up where it does not belong.

spells.name: Undertow
spells.blurb: The pull that takes strong swimmers, applied on dry land.

spells.name: Taste the Salt
spells.blurb: Working magic leaves brine on the tongue; this is how you notice.

spells.name: Settle the Debt
spells.blurb: Paying off somebody else's working, at your own cost.

spells.name: Ask the Drowned
spells.blurb: They answer. They are not always pleased to be asked.

spells.name: Long Lung
spells.blurb: The working every salvage crew wishes it could afford twice a day.

spells.name: Cut the Line
spells.blurb: Severing the pull before it finishes taking someone. Costly, and it is noticed.

spells.name: Reed-quiet
spells.blurb: Crossing a marsh without leaving the bent stems that say you did.

items.name: Gutting Blade
items.blurb: A fish knife that got ambitious.

items.name: Rope Axe
items.blurb: For cutting a line fast when the line is about to kill somebody.

items.name: Channel Spear
items.blurb: Long-hafted for fishing, wading, and the occasional argument.

items.name: Wading Fork
items.blurb: Three tines, for flounder and for footing.

items.name: Quay Bow
items.blurb: Short-armed for shooting from a boat that will not stay still.

items.name: Sounding Pole
items.blurb: For finding the bottom, and for reminding people you found it.

items.name: Bait Knife
items.blurb: Everyone on this coast has one and nobody thinks of it as a weapon.

items.name: Oilskins
items.blurb: Waxed and reeking, and the only reason you are not hypothermic.

items.name: Salvage Rig
items.blurb: Reinforced diving leathers with the buckles a wreck-diver can find blind.

items.name: Netmail
items.blurb: Fine rings under a jerkin. It will drown you, and everyone wears it anyway.

items.name: Warden's Plate
items.blurb: Overlapping scale, issued by a treasury that no longer pays wages.

items.name: Hatch Board
items.blurb: A boat hatch with a grip nailed on. It floats, which has saved lives.

features.name: Breaking Water
features.blurb: The cold fury of somebody who has watched the sea take enough.

features.name: Surfacing
features.blurb: The gasp that means you are not finished yet.

features.name: Working Song
features.blurb: The rhythm that gets a rope hauled and a crew home.

features.name: Toll the Bell
features.blurb: The deep water pays attention for exactly as long as the note holds.

features.name: Take the Marsh's Shape
features.blurb: Borrowing a body the fen already keeps on hand.

features.name: Warm the Cold
features.blurb: Bringing somebody back from the temperature the water left them at.

features.name: Known Water
features.blurb: Years spent learning how one kind of thing moves in a channel.

monsters.name: Sluice Rat
monsters.blurb: Lives in the drains and is not afraid of a lamp.

monsters.name: Culvert Swarm
monsters.blurb: The drain is moving and it is moving toward you.

monsters.name: Marsh Leech
monsters.blurb: Flies badly, latches perfectly.

monsters.name: Wreck-picker
monsters.blurb: Got to the salvage first and would rather you had not.

monsters.name: Salvage Boss
monsters.blurb: Runs a crew, a boat, and three sets of books.

monsters.name: Quay Watch
monsters.blurb: Underpaid, overworked, and privately on your side.

monsters.name: Channel Runner
monsters.blurb: Knows every route through the reeds and sells that knowledge carefully.

monsters.name: Old Tidewarden
monsters.blurb: Held the wall for twenty years and has the joints to prove it.

monsters.name: Breakwater Raider
monsters.blurb: From a town the sea already took, with nothing left to lose.

monsters.name: Deep-water Debtor
monsters.blurb: Signed something at low tide and is recruiting to cover the interest.

monsters.name: Reed Adder
monsters.blurb: Green on green, and it was there before you stepped.

monsters.name: Channel Lurker
monsters.blurb: A log until it is not.

monsters.name: Stilt-house Spider
monsters.blurb: Nests in the pilings, under the floor you are standing on.

monsters.name: Marsh Dog
monsters.blurb: Gone feral from a drowned town, still half expecting to be fed.

monsters.name: Gull-wife
monsters.blurb: Sings the working songs back at you, slightly wrong.

monsters.name: Low-water Shade
monsters.blurb: Only present between the tides, which is when it does its work.

monsters.name: Salt-bones
monsters.blurb: Scoured white and still wearing its boots.

monsters.name: The Returned
monsters.blurb: The water gave one back. It walked home.

monsters.name: Flat-crawler
monsters.blurb: Works the tide flats for the same things the mudlarks do.

monsters.name: Bell-shade
monsters.blurb: Rings for a town that is not there to hear it.

monsters.name: Drowned Warden
monsters.blurb: Still holding a wall that failed eleven years ago.

monsters.name: The Spring Tide
monsters.blurb: The water, briefly, with an opinion.

monsters.name: Marsh Lantern
monsters.blurb: It wants you to follow it and you know that, and you will anyway.

monsters.name: Fen-troll
monsters.blurb: Wet, patient, and it heals faster than you can argue.

monsters.name: Channel Hydra
monsters.blurb: The reason nobody dredges the deep cut any more.

monsters.name: The Thing in the Cut
monsters.blurb: Older than the town, and it remembers being paid tribute.

monsters.name: The Debt Come Due
monsters.blurb: It has your family name and it is not in a hurry.

factions.name: The Tidewardens
factions.blurb: The seawall garrison, unpaid since spring and holding the line anyway, mostly.

factions.name: The Salvage Guilds
factions.blurb: They price a town's timber while people still live in it, and they are never late.

factions.name: The Bell-keepers
factions.blurb: They count the drowned and ring for them. They know more than they say.

factions.name: The Deep Water
factions.blurb: Not a faction so much as a creditor. It lends, and it collects.

factions.name: The Channel-kin Moots
factions.blurb: The old reptilian councils of the waterways, who have watched three human coasts come and go.

locations.name: Old Fennow
locations.blurb: A stilt-town with three years of dry land left, arguing about which three.

locations.name: The Seawall
locations.blurb: Nine miles of piled stone that is winning in some places and losing in others.

locations.name: The Deep Cut
locations.blurb: A dredged channel nobody dredges any more, and nobody will say why.

locations.name: Marrow Quay
locations.blurb: Where the salvage comes ashore and gets sorted by people who do not ask.

locations.name: The Drowned Fields
locations.blurb: Farmland eleven years under. At low water the field walls still show.

locations.name: Gannet Rock
locations.blurb: A lamp on a stone, one keeper, and a very long night.

locations.name: The Reed Country
locations.blurb: Miles of green with paths only the runners know, and they charge.

hooks: The bell of a town that drowned eleven years ago has started ringing at low water, and it is ringing the count for a funeral that has not happened yet.
The Tidewardens have not been paid since spring. Half of them have taken salvage work, and the salvage guild is the reason the wage stopped.
A wreck-diver came up from the Deep Cut with a sealed strongbox and no memory of the last four hours.
Someone in Old Fennow is quietly selling the town's foundation timber, one pile at a time, and the next spring tide will find out who.
A Channel-kin moot has issued a formal claim on the Drowned Fields, and it is a much older claim than the deeds anyone else is holding.
A family the party owes a favour to has just been marked as debt-bearing, and the terms name a date three weeks out.
The keeper of Gannet Rock has not signalled for six nights, and the lamp is still lit.

glossary.meaning: The whole sinking coast, and by extension the people stubborn enough to stay on it.
A bargain struck with the deep water. Always honoured, rarely on the terms the borrower expected.
The hours when the flats are walkable, the drowned are closest, and most business gets done.
The grey coastal fog that arrives in minutes and hides anything.
The legal claim on a wreck. Enforced by guilds, ignored by everyone poor.
Someone the water took and then gave back. Not the same afterwards, and treated carefully.
Driving foundations into mud. Brutal, well paid, and the reason half the March has bad hands.
Tolling once for each of the drowned. It is how a town admits how bad it was.
Any dredged deep channel, but usually the Deep Cut, and usually said quietly.
What happens to a caster who draws more than the water will lend.
